question.prompt: What is the value of the following expression? \[\dfrac{\log_2 80}{\log_{40}2}-\dfrac{\log_2 160}{\log_{20}2}\]

solutions.title: Use one logarithm
solutions.explanation:
Changing the denominator logarithms to base \(2\) lets us express every term using a single unknown logarithm.

By the change-of-base formula,
\[
\log_{40}2=\frac{\log_2 2}{\log_2 40}=\frac1{\log_2 40},
\qquad
\log_{20}2=\frac1{\log_2 20}.
\]
Thus the expression becomes
\[
(\log_2 80)(\log_2 40)-(\log_2 160)(\log_2 20).
\]
Let \(t=\log_2 5\). The product rule for logarithms gives \(\log_2(2^k\cdot5)=k+t\), so
\[
\log_2 80=4+t,\quad \log_2 40=3+t,
\]
\[
\log_2 160=5+t,\quad \log_2 20=2+t.
\]
Substituting and expanding, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
(4+t)(3+t)-(5+t)(2+t)
&=(12+7t+t^2)-(10+7t+t^2)\\
&=2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The value is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
